the institutional profiles of the 28 institutions in our study show that the institutions are active in both intra and cross-sector networks and that they are active in networks with different rationales, different knowledge trajectories and different types of knowledge.

‘Institutions of higher education in different national systems vary in their positioning in relation to knowledge networks, with the most active in cross-sector networks being those with a public mission and knowledge as a public good.’

The diversity of higher education institutions, as revealed by our comparative grid analysis, is a function of their different missions in respect of their knowledge production and knowledge dissemination roles and their different domains of operation.

the ways in which the knowledge trajectories of different kinds of higher institutions are shaped within networks, as these institutions interact with one another and with other organisations and actors in society.
